title: fix(lint): filter-token-unknown states the runtime's refusal, FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN / 400
body:
Fixes #24293

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`filter-token-unknown`'s message said an unresolvable filter placeholder "is sent to the data engine as a literal string, matches no record, and the surface renders empty". The runtime does not do that: the data engine refuses a query that carries one, `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400. The message now says so:

```text
Filter value "{current_user}" is not a resolvable placeholder. The data engine refuses a query that carries it (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`, 400), so the surface never shows the data the filter meant.
```

Message and comment text only. Unchanged: the rule id, severity (`error`), `path`, `hint`, and which values the rule reports. The message's first sentence is unchanged, so the negative pin at `validate-filter-tokens.test.ts` (the `{record_id}` refusal must not read as an unknown spelling) still guards the same text.

## Every site of the false sentence, on base `21070a2f0a`

| site | done |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/lint/src/validate-filter-tokens.ts:236`–`:237`, the message | rewritten as above |
| `validate-filter-tokens.ts:25`–`:26`, the module header ("passed to the data engine **verbatim**, matches no row") | rewritten: the engine refuses the query, naming `UnknownFilterTokenError` in `@objectstack/core` |
| `validate-filter-tokens.ts:28`–`:41`, the header's "Why this is an error" section ("The runtime failure mode is silent", present tense) | put in the past tense: the silent zero is what the rule was written against, before the runtime resolved placeholders. Says why the rule stays an error now that the runtime refuses: the refusal arrives only when a surface is opened, after the build passed, which an AI author's author, validate, correct loop never sees |
| `validate-filter-tokens.ts:106`, the `severity` field doc ("silently matches nothing") | rewritten: the engine refuses a query carrying an unresolvable placeholder |
| `packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-references.ts:36`–`:39`, the docblock quoting the old message (triage `6248475229`) | corrected. The quote is gone, and the comparison it carried is inverted: the value `filter-token-unknown` reports is refused loudly, while a dangling field path at the same node is the quiet failure, per that file's own severity note |
| `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:917`–`:920`, the comment above `validateFilterTokens`' registration ("reaches the data engine as a literal and matches nothing. The surface renders empty with no error"). The comment ships inside `@objectstack/lint`'s `dist/index.js` and `dist/runtime.js` | rewritten in `f3d1666d9`, comment text only. The claim's file surface was amended to add it (`6249110232`). The `#3574` provenance and the silent-zero history are kept, in the past tense, as in the module header. Before and after are below |

The `authoring-rules.ts` comment before (`21070a2f0`, `:917`–`:920`):

```text
  // #3574 — a filter value like `{current_user}` resolves in no vocabulary,
  // reaches the data engine as a literal and matches nothing. The surface
  // renders empty with no error, and a silent zero is indistinguishable from a
  // genuine one at review time.
```

and after (`f3d1666d9`, `:917`–`:921`):

```text
  // #3574 — a filter value like `{current_user}` resolves in no vocabulary. The
  // data engine refuses a query carrying it (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`, 400). When
  // #3574 was filed it reached the engine as a literal and matched nothing: the
  // surface rendered empty with no error, a silent zero indistinguishable from a
  // genuine one at review time.
```

`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` (`os explain filter-token-unknown`, from #24292) already says "the data engine refuses the query (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`, 400) rather than compare the placeholder as a literal string, so the surface never shows the data the filter meant". The new message takes its words, so the two agree. That file is not touched.

## What the runtime does, read on base `21070a2f0a`

- `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`: `resolveFilterTokens` throws `UnknownFilterTokenError` (`status = 400`, `code = 'FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN'`) for a whole-string placeholder outside both vocabularies (`:547`), and for one the resolver drops (`:552`).
- Callers: the ObjectQL engine on every read verb (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, through `resolveWhereTokens`) and on `update` / `delete` (`withResolvedWhere`); the analytics service on `where`, `timeDimensions[].dateRange` and a dataset's own filter and measure filters (`analytics-service.ts:1852`–`:1883`, `dataset-executor.ts:128`).
- Pins: `packages/objectql/src/engine-filter-token-today-spelling.test.ts:71`–`:74` (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400) and `packages/rest/src/rest-aggregate-positions.test.ts:171`, which asserts `_status` 400 and `code` `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` at `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` for a `where` carrying `'{not_a_token}'`.
- objectui's client resolver (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts` there, `resolveContextTokens`) passes an unknown token through untouched, so it reaches the server and is refused there.
- The message claims the engine's door only, and its claim is conditional ("refuses a query that carries it"). A surface whose filter never becomes a server query is outside the claim. The one such door this read found is in Acceptance notes.

## Tests

On head `f3d1666d9` (round 1's `6be194c50`, plus the `authoring-rules.ts` comment commit):

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/lint...' build` (lint and its build closure): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The old sentence's phrases ("reaches the data engine as a literal", "renders empty with no error", "sent to the data engine as a literal string", "passed to the data engine", "matches no record, and the surface renders empty", "unresolved placeholder silently matches nothing") have 0 hits in `packages/lint/src` and 0 in `packages/lint/dist`. The controls hit: the new comment's "data engine refuses a query carrying it" (src 1, dist 4 files) and the new message (dist 4 files).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 144 passed (144)`, `Tests 6858 passed (6858)`. The 5 cases that `6be194c50`'s run skipped (`6853 passed | 5 skipped`) are the `skipIf` cases in `lazy-deps.test.ts` and `runtime-lazy-deps.test.ts`. They need lint's own built `dist/`, which that run did not have. This time they ran, against the rebuilt `dist/`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `check:test-typecheck: OK`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists `validate-filter-tokens.test.ts`, so the test layer compiles the new case.
- New case in `validate-filter-tokens.test.ts`: "names the code the data engine refuses the query with, near miss or not". It holds both arms of the unknown-token finding (a near miss `{current_user}`, and `{whoever_is_watching}` with none) to the named code `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`, not to the prose around it.
- No test pinned the old prose. A repo-wide `git grep` for its phrases ("literal string, matches no", "surface renders empty", "sent to the data engine", "passed to the data engine", "is not a resolvable placeholder") (plus "reaches the data engine as a literal") outside the changeset, which quotes the old text as its FROM, finds only the kept first sentence and the negative pin above. The same grep over objectui at `32b492b67` finds nothing. `packages/cli/test/authoring-rule-command-parity.test.ts:107` names the rule id only.
- Ablation, one-off, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit x1 to x0, blob `47d8294046cf` to `a81f9a88dae0`): with `` (`FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`, 400) `` removed from the message, `Tests 1 failed | 33 passed (34)`, failing on exactly the new case: `expected 'Filter value "{current_user}" is not …' to contain` the code. Restored: blob equals HEAD (`47d8294046cf`), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean. The test imports the source by relative path, so no `dist/` sits between the mutation and the run.

## Gates (local subset; the whole farm is CI's)

Derived on head `f3d1666d9` with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths given (change set: these 5 files vs merge base `21070a2f0`). That gives 64 commands, the same set as on `6be194c50`, and 11 more than the claim's path-only lead of 53. The extra 11 are the changeset-kind families. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and the record was reconciled with `--ran`: "64 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)", exit 0.

- 62 exited 0, `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift` among them, since lint's `dist/` was built this time. On `6be194c50`, 61 exited 0 on the first pass. These include `check:nul-bytes`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` and `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`.
- `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift`: on `6be194c50` it exited 3 on the first pass (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: no `packages/lint/dist`), then 0 after a lint build. On `f3d1666d9` it exited 0: "4 declared transcript value(s) across 417 page(s) under content/docs/ equal what the registry derives today, and no undeclared block quotes one". The built `dist/index.js` carries the new message, and the old sentence is gone from it (0 hits).
- NOT MEASURED, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3): `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs every package's `dist/` (a whole `pnpm build`), and `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` needs `@objectstack/objectql`'s `dist/`. Both are left to CI.
- `origin/main` has moved past the base (`2ee5861b0`, `0c3db0f6a`, `30da04f8e` and later). None of these commits touches `packages/lint`, its build closure, or `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`. The branch is not merged with them, as the patch round directs, and CI runs on GitHub's merge ref. The derivation on `f3d1666d9` flags 4 gate inputs that changed on `main` across that range: `scripts/check-single-authz-resolver.mjs`, `scripts/slot-lookup-baseline.json`, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` and one `scripts/adr-anchors/` file. Their local readings are of the base's copies, and CI's readings on the merge ref are the ones that count.

## Acceptance notes

- **objectui's in-memory `ValueDataSource`** (`provider: 'value'`, `packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts` at objectui `32b492b67`) evaluates a filter on the client and sends no query, so no engine refuses there. Its matcher has no placeholder handling, so a literal `{…}` compares as a string. This is read from code, NOT MEASURED. The new message does not claim that door, because its claim is conditional on a query reaching the engine.
- The REST refusal is cited from the existing pin (`rest-aggregate-positions.test.ts:171`), not re-run here. CI's `Test Core` runs it.
